catalog_quote: 14. Es kommen mindestens zwei dynamische Akzente in drei- und mehrsilbigen Wörtern zur Anwendung, indem der Hauptton zum Nebenton wird, wenn eine Repetition des Stammes eintritt oder wenn eine Endung den Hauptton auf sich zieht: mṓli »Faden«, mṑlimṓli »Fadenspiel«, ibál »er fällt«, ibàlbèhé »er wird nicht fallen«. Sonst aber ist keine Regel ersichtlich — auch nicht aus Länge oder Kürze der Vokale — welche der drei letzten Silben den Hauptton bevorzugt; mehr als zwei Silben bleiben nie unbetont. [p. 235] Durch die Tonverschiebungen — über welche einige Regeln später angeführt werden — erhält die gesprochene Rede häufig einen eigentümlichen, trochäisch-anapästischen Rhythmus, bei dem das Herauserkennen der Stammsilben erschwert ist ... 15. Abgesehen von dem erwähnten musikalischen Tonfall im Satz war ein Hoch- oder Tiefton eines Vokals — etwa um dem Wort dadurch eine andere Bedeutung oder eine neue grammatische Form zu geben — nicht zu entdecken.

new_statements.translation: 14. At least two dynamic (stress) accents are used in words of three or more syllables, the main stress becoming a secondary stress when the stem is reduplicated or when an ending draws the main stress onto itself: móli 'thread', mòlimóli 'string figure', ibál 'he falls', ibàlbehé 'he will not fall'. Otherwise, however, no rule is discernible — not from the length or shortness of the vowels either — as to which of the last three syllables is preferred for the main stress; more than two syllables never remain unstressed. [...] 15. Apart from the musical sentence intonation mentioned, a high or low tone on a vowel — e.g. to give the word a different meaning or a new grammatical form — could not be detected.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Main (dynamic) stress falls on one of the last three syllables of the word, but which one is not predictable by any rule Dempwolff could find (vowel length is not the conditioner); stress is marked lexically with accents throughout his texts and vocabulary. Certain suffixes attract main stress (e.g. 3pl possessive -ndin; 1sg/1pl/2pl possessed forms stress the stem-final vowel), and the suffixless 2sg possessed form retracts stress to the penult or antepenult; under reduplication or stress-attracting suffixation the original main stress survives as secondary. No lexical or grammatical tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Words of 3+ syllables have at least two stresses; a demoted Hauptton becomes Nebenton under reduplication/suffixation; rhythmic constraint: never more than two consecutive unstressed syllables ('trochaic-anapaestic rhythm', p.235). Par. 21 p.236: 'independent' body-part forms are stressed on the final syllable with secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Morphological stress shifts with possessive suffixes (par. 19, p.236): -ndin (3pl) attracts main stress; 1sg, both 1pl and 2pl forms put main stress on the stem-final vowel; 3sg usage varies; suffixless 2sg form retracts to penult or antepenult (tamánu 'my father', táma 'your father'). Vocabulary preamble: where accent marks are absent, stress was not securely determined. The later SIL OPD (archives 42518, n.d., 2-week workshop) only says 'Stress can occur at least on first and second syllables. No futher analysis available.'
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement from dictated texts and elicited words (citation and connected speech); Dempwolff separately notes sentence-level 'musikalischer Tonfall' (intonation) and explicitly denies lexical tone. Data from six young male speakers recorded in Dar es Salaam in 1906, i.e. Bilibil Island speech of c.1900.
new_statements.identity_note: Dempwolff 1909 describes 'die Sprache von Bilibili', i.e. the language of Bilibil (Bilbil) Island in Astrolabe Bay, Kaiser-Wilhelms-Land — the same community as Glottolog bilb1241 Bilibil / ISO brz Bilbil (the Bilbil later resettled on the adjacent mainland near Madang). His data: texts and elicitation from six c.18-year-old Bilibil men (chief consultant Ngomu) recorded in Dar es Salaam, March-April 1906. The SIL OPD (archives 42518) is headed 'Bilibil Language [BRZ] Madang – Madang Province', major village Bilibil; same languoid.
